**Stable, published under the npm `latest` dist-tag.** A plain
`npm install @candid-core/schema` selects this version once it is published;
`beta` stays on 0.3.0-beta.1. Until 1.0, any release may change the builder
API, the inferred domain types, the codec's wire behaviour, and the codes and
`$`-rooted paths validation reports. Pin an exact version.

`@candid-core/schema` 0.3 breaks the 0.2 API (principal values are canonical text, collapsing opts are boxed, every `vec nat8` is a `Uint8Array`, generated modules use a new binding layout and may omit declarations, and the `./actor`, `./transport-icp`, `./forms` and `./labels` subpaths are gone); there is no compatibility layer.

That line is the 0.3 line's, unchanged: 0.4.0 breaks nothing in 0.3.0's API.

## Installation

```sh
npm install --save-exact @candid-core/schema@0.4.0
```

The generator that emits modules for this release is `@candid-core/cli`
0.3.0, which declares this package as an optional peer at exactly `0.4.0`:

```sh
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @candid-core/cli@0.3.0
```

## What an app on 0.3.0 / 0.2.0 does

1. Move both packages in one step, each at its exact version, with the two
   lines above. npm refuses a mismatched pair (`ERESOLVE could not
   resolve`): CLI 0.2.0 peers schema exactly `0.3.0`, and CLI 0.3.0 peers
   exactly `0.4.0`.
2. Run `candid-core-cli gen` again over every committed module. The module
   text changes (below), so `gen --check` reports each module CLI 0.2.0
   wrote as drifted, exit 1, until it is regenerated. The envelopes do not
   change.
3. Nothing else. Code written against 0.3.0 compiles and runs unchanged
   against 0.4.0, and a module CLI 0.2.0 generated compiles against it too.
   The one type-level difference a consumer can see is in regenerated
   modules: a method type of `Actor` is its call signature intersected with
   `$.WithMode<mode>`, so a test that compares it for exact equality with
   the bare signature (an `Equal<A, B>` helper) now fails, while
   `Parameters<>`, `ReturnType<>`, `keyof Actor` and an implementation by a
   plain async function are unchanged.

[Migrating from 0.3.0](https://b3hr4d.github.io/candid-core/migrating-from-0-3.html)
has the same steps, with the compiler's errors.

## Pairing

- **`candid-core`**: pairs with `0.1.0-beta.3` (crates.io), as 0.3.0 did.
  Every Contract document `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3 writes loads in this
  release, so the README's `cargo install candid-core --version
  0.1.0-beta.3` then `candid-core compile --envelope` on-ramp produces
  documents this release loads. No crate release is needed first. The
  repository's `candid-core` source has five changes over that archive: the
  four 0.3.0 listed (a leading UTF-8 byte order mark accepted, #176; a run of
  more than 256 consecutive comments refused, #219; a type on a cycle
  through `opt` alone refused by the compiler, #234; a struct written as a
  JSON array refused by the Contract loaders, #235) and, since 0.3.0, a unit
  variant written as a JSON map refused by the Contract loaders (#238,
  #243). None moves a Contract or an identity of an input both 0.1.0-beta.3
  and this source accept. This package's loader changed for none of the
  five: it already refused the map form (`"primitive": {"nat64": null}`
  gives `invalid_contract_document` at `$.types[n].primitive`, "unknown
  primitive type", measured on this release's `dist`).
- **Generator**: the `candid-core-ts` generator is unpublishable on crates.io;
  it reaches consumers only inside `@candid-core/cli`. The generator revision
  this release pairs with is the one `@candid-core/cli` 0.3.0 embeds: the
  commit both packages are dispatched from, recorded in each run.
- **Lockstep**: the CLI peers this exact version, and is published right
  after it.

## Public API against 0.3.0

The previous stable release. Exported names of the shipped `dist/*.d.ts`,
0.3.0 (rebuilt from its `gitHead`, `acabe0fcfbd8019d14e2c2550c5e6cd872a3529a`;
the rebuilt tarball's shasum, `edaa7318baef96e7ed1f21959592f0c031ac7489`,
and SHA-512 integrity, `sha512-4dvVrkIcU/YXFQv8…`, equal the registry's)
against this release, with the comment-stripped declaration text of every
kept name compared. Nothing is marked **BREAKING**: nothing breaks.

Export map: `.`, `./validate`, `./contract`, `./codec`, unchanged. No
dependency and no peer, as before.

| Entry | Name | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.` | `WithMode<M extends MethodMode>` | added: an interface with one optional property under a `unique symbol` no value has, so a method's mode is carried in the type system only |
| `.` | `ModeOf<F>` | added: the mode a method type carries through `WithMode`, or the whole `MethodMode` union when it carries none |

Kept with identical declaration text: all 29 names of `.`, all 14 of
`./validate`, all 12 of `./contract`, and all 17 of `./codec` (29 → 31,
14, 12, 17). `validate.d.ts`, `contract.d.ts`, `codec.d.ts` and the four
internal modules' declarations are byte-identical to 0.3.0's; `schema.d.ts`
grows from 734 lines to 764 with the two declarations and their
documentation, and one documentation comment (`Schema`'s, which quotes the
generated line) changes. Every shipped `.js` file is byte-identical to
0.3.0's except `schema.js`, whose one difference is that same comment in
source form. So no verdict, byte, issue code or path can differ.

## Generated modules, which this package types

`@candid-core/cli` 0.3.0's generator, the release this one pairs with,
changes two things about the modules it writes. Neither changes this
package's API.

- **Each method of `Actor` carries its mode**:
  `fee: (() => Promise<Tokens>) & $.WithMode<"query">`. `ModeOf` reads it
  back, so a call layer can refuse an update where it builds a read, at
  compile time. A module with an actor method imports `WithMode` and so
  needs this release: against 0.3.0 it fails with `TS2694` ("Namespace …
  has no exported member 'WithMode'"), once per method (measured with a
  two-method service compiled against the registry's 0.3.0).
- **Each type is declared under its Candid name**, `export type Account =
  …`, with the schema bound as the local `$Account`, so a compiler error
  names `Account` rather than `$Account`. A name that cannot be a type in
  the module keeps the `$` local for its type too: the four global types
  the generated types use (`Array`, `Promise`, `Record`, `Uint8Array`) and
  62 words TypeScript refuses as a type's name (`delete`, `string`,
  `default`, `keyof`, …).

## Known limitations and deferred work

- `validate` (and `encode`'s value walk) charge each examined record or
  variant key against `maxElements`, which candid-core's
  `validate_host_value` does not, so a record-shaped value reaches the
  element bound before candid-core's, and a value `decode` returns can need
  a larger `maxElements` in `validate` (#241, an open owner call; today's
  behaviour ships).
- Declarations whose records canonicalize to one node share its field
  names, so a declaration can get another's spelling (#229; documented and
  deferred by decision, because the fix changes the Contract format).
- A Contract document without a `declarations` key is refused, which
  `Contract::from_json` accepts (#228); the refusal is kept by decision.
- A Contract that already holds a type on a cycle through `opt` alone,
  written by hand or by `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3, still loads, and
  decoding a non-`opt` value at it ends in a `value_depth` refusal; the
  compiler, and so `candid-core-cli gen`, refuses such a type (#234).
- Refusing `Infinity` as a limit may be revisited before 1.0 (#190).
- NaN payload bits are not preserved by the `number` domain (#178).
- Two structurally equal record declarations still collapse to the first
  name in generated modules (#197, "Not yet scheduled").

## Irreversibility

An npm version number is permanent: once published it can be deprecated, but
never republished with other bytes. A defect in this release is fixed by the
next one, which a new CLI release then pairs with.
